E1.evidence: Issue #863 gives reproduction steps ("fastdds discovery -i 1 -l 127.0.0.1 -p 11888", then "ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER=\"127.0.0.1:11888\" ros2 run demo_nodes_cpp talker" / "... listener") and the observed result "The listener can not receive messages from the talker." A maintainer diagnosed it: "service id for discovery server is mapped to the semi-colon based index offset in `ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER`." https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/863

units_identified: Fast DDS discovery server (fastdds discovery, server id 1)
demo_nodes_cpp talker/listener using rmw_fastrtps_cpp as discovery-server clients
E2.evidence: The resolving change only binds the server address at deployment through the ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER environment variable; no unit's interface changed. Maintainer: "can you try if `ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER=\";127.0.0.1:11888\"` works?"; reporter: "Yes. It can work. So the format of ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER depend on service ID. ... It is not an issue." The only code change is documentation (ros2_documentation #6107/#6108): "For ``--server-id 1``: ``ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER=\";127.0.0.1:11888\"``" and "If the server ID doesn't match the position in the environment variable, clients will not be able to connect to the server."

E3.evidence: PAIR: the talker and listener each connect as clients to the discovery server; the failure is at discovery, so the listener never matches the talker.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "The listener can not receive messages from the talker." and "Once service ID is changed to 0, listener can receive messages."

ineligible_reason: deployment_wiring: clients must list a discovery server with --server-id N at position N of the semicolon-separated ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER variable; the fix is the environment-variable value (and documentation), with no interface change in any unit.
notes: Reported on humble and jazzy with rmw_fastrtps_cpp 6.2.9 (humble); reporter: "The same testing steps did not have any issues in the Kilted version." Maintainer: "I think somewhere during developing kilted version fast-dds addresses this constrain" (not verified here). A second documentation defect was raised in the same thread: "The `fastdds discovery` command does not have the \"--ip-address\" argument. But document also used it. It should be `--udp-address` or `--tcp-address`." (a CLI usage mismatch between the tutorial and the fastdds tool), also fixed by #6107/#6108 (merged 2025-12-19 into jazzy and humble). The issue was closed by the reporter as not an issue.
